title: Agent rules protocol
description: The agent_rules extension point's call (version 1, #16820; docs/extensions/extensions.md "Agent rules"): when the manager starts a new task Agent it asks each agent_rules contribution that is on for the rules that Agent should start with, given its agent type, launcher, model, directory and computer. A non-empty text goes in as its own block with the task's other framework rules (task_instructions). Only the manager calls, once per new start and never for a resumed Agent; every call is bounded in time and size, and an answer over a limit or of the wrong shape is dropped whole, never cut. A failure leaves that contribution's rules out of this start; the start itself never fails or waits past the bound because of it. Errors are the base ErrorCode with a one-line message for people. Plugin-side: only the hub and the program speak it.

AgentRulesForStartParams.description: agent_rules.for_start: the rules for one new task Agent. Read-only: answering changes nothing the manager can see; the program may record that it was asked.

agent.description: The agent type the resolved launcher starts (claude, codex, agy, pi, opencode, or a runtime's own type).

launcher.description: The launcher's name on that computer.

model.description: The model id the Agent starts on, as the start names it (it may carry a context-window suffix such as [1m]); empty when the start uses the launcher's own default and the manager cannot tell which model that is.

cwd.description: The Agent's directory on its computer, as the task names it (before any worktree the Agent makes itself).

machine.description: The id of the computer the Agent starts on.

AgentRulesForStartResult.description: The rules for that Agent. An empty text adds nothing.

text.description: The rules, as the Agent should read them. At most 4096 bytes of UTF-8: the manager drops a longer answer whole.

rev.description: The program's own version of the text (a hash, say), logged with the start so a later look can tell which rules an Agent had.
